issues.claim: W1.depends_on lists "W3b" as a soft dependency (mode-1 timed-signature surface), implying it is one of the batch's sibling work items to be checked against.
issues.actual: No W3b.json exists under /etheron-pod/mini-consensus-lean/rollout/designs/ (only W1, W2, W3a, W4, W5, W6, W7 = 7 total items, i.e. 6 real siblings to W1, not 7). W3b is referenced only as unscheduled future work inside W1, W2 and W3a's prose (grep confirms no design file; designs-partial/W3b-run3.md is an abandoned salvage, not a committed design). The task framing "against the other seven items" is therefore off by one against what actually exists in docs/rollout/designs/.
issues.fix: No change needed to W1 itself — its own text already says 'Soft only' and correctly treats W3b as non-blocking/hypothetical. Note for the orchestrator: the current batch has 6 siblings to W1 (W2, W3a, W4, W5, W6, W7), not 7; W3b is not a landable item in this round.

issues.claim: touches_existing for W1 is the minimal permitted set (two import lines each in MoltPetit.lean and Molt.lean).
issues.actual: True in isolation and confirmed against the live files (MoltPetit.lean has 34 existing import lines added incrementally the same way; Molt.lean has 9). But three OTHER batch items independently target the exact same textual insertion point in MoltPetit.lean — W3a, W5, and W6 all specify inserting their new import line(s) 'after `import MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingScheduleTimed`, before `import MoltPetit.Model.KeyRotationTests`'. All seven batch items (including W1) touch the same two root files. This is not a semantic conflict (Lean import order is irrelevant to elaboration) but will produce trivial textual merge conflicts if two of these land close together without a rebase.
issues.fix: No redesign needed. Whoever lands second among {W3a, W5, W6} (and, more loosely, any pair among all 7 items) just needs a one-line rebase of MoltPetit.lean/Molt.lean; call this out to the human/agent doing the actual landing sequence rather than to the design authors.

confirmed_reuses: MoltPetit.lean and Molt.lean current contents read directly: confirms the 'add N import lines' touches_existing pattern is the established repo idiom (34 and 9 pre-existing import lines respectively), not a smuggled edit.

Molt.lean imports MoltPetit.* modules (e.g. Molt/Rotation.lean imports MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingLockstep, KeyStealingCert, KeyStealingScheduleCert); grep over MoltPetit/*.lean and MoltPetit.lean finds zero `import Molt.` lines — confirms 'Molt imports MoltPetit, never the reverse' as claimed.

MoltPetit/Model/KeyStealingLockstep.lean:84 `theorem lockstepOk_iff_pairwise` is public; the nearby `lockstep_rel` (172) and `lockstep_const` (195) are `private theorem` — confirms the design's claim that it must build its public `lockstepOk_append_iff` from the public iff-lemma rather than reuse-and-expose the private helpers (no visibility-widening edit to the existing file needed or proposed).

MoltPetit/Model/KeyStealingLockstep.lean: validSignedChainLock, LockstepPackage.toPackageA, lockstep_declares_rosterGen, lockstep_validSignedChainSched all exist substantially where cited (spot-checked by grep/sed; exact line numbers drift by a few lines from the cited ones but the declarations and their content are present and match the claimed shapes).

No design in the batch (W2, W3a, W4, W5, W6, W7) creates or touches MoltPetit/Model/KeyStealingLockstepCert.lean, Molt/LockstepCert.lean, or any file W1 creates — confirmed by grep across all sibling design JSONs.

No design in the batch defines a structure/inductive/def with the same name as any of W1's three new_defs (lockstepFrom, GroundedCertLock, GroundedHistoryLock) — confirmed by extracting new_defs name lists from all 7 design JSONs; nearest neighbour is W5's LockstepPackageGen/LockstepPackageTimed/NoPrematureTheftLock, which are distinct names for a distinct (per-generation census) engine.

W5.json's own depends_on/enables entries for W1 ('No dependency... Build order between W1 and W5 is free', and the enables entry describing a hypothetical future W1×W5 join) are consistent with, and do not contradict, W1.json's depends_on/enables entries for W5 — cross-checked both directions.

W4.json's enables entry for W1 ('SyncInductionData... could reuse... Not required reading for W1/W5, noted only as a reuse opportunity') and W1.json's enables entry for W4 are consistent, soft, and non-contradictory in both directions.
W2.json explicitly states 'Not a dependency either way' with respect to W1, matching that W1.json does not list W2 in either depends_on or enables — no contradiction.
W6.json and W7.json contain no reference to W1 at all, consistent with W1 listing no dependency on or enablement of either.

CertClaim (the structure GroundedCertLock's index type) is explicitly flagged in W1's own open_questions as 'cannot be extended (existing definition)' — the design does not add a field to it; g is carried as separate inductive/theorem state, not as a smuggled CertClaim field.
ordering_notes: W1 is additively well-isolated: its only touches_existing are import-line insertions into the two root files, which is the repo's established idiom (confirmed by reading MoltPetit.lean/Molt.lean directly) and is the same pattern every other batch item (W2, W3a, W4, W5, W6, W7) also uses — so W1 is not an outlier in permitted-touch style, though see the merge-friction note in issues. No sibling design creates, imports, or edits any file W1 creates (KeyStealingLockstepCert.lean, Results/LockstepCertAxioms.lean, Molt/LockstepCert.lean, Molt/LockstepCertAxioms.lean), and no sibling defines a structure with the same name as W1's GroundedCertLock/GroundedHistoryLock/lockstepFrom — no loop risk, no 'who should own it' question arises because nobody else claims this territory. W1's stated dependencies are both soft (W5, and the non-existent-in-this-batch W3b) and its stated enablements (W5, W4) are corroborated by those items' own design text in both directions — the graph is consistent and acyclic. Because every real consumption is through opaque hypotheses (hP : LockstepPackage, existing public lemmas from KeyStealingLockstep.lean/KeyStealingScheduleCert.lean that no sibling touches), W1 would NOT need redoing regardless of which of W2/W3a/W4/W5/W6/W7 lands first or last, and none of them would need redoing if W1 lands first — landing order among these 7 items is free with respect to W1. The one genuine friction is cosmetic: W3a, W5 and W6 all specify literally the same insertion line in MoltPetit.lean for their own imports, which will cause trivial (non-semantic) git conflicts if landed back-to-back without rebasing; this is a batch-wide characteristic (all 7 items touch the same 2 root files) rather than a defect specific to W1's design.
revised_effort: No change from the design's own estimate (2-3 sessions, ~720 lines) is warranted by this ordering review; the only follow-up cost is a possible one-line rebase of MoltPetit.lean/Molt.lean if W1 lands near W3a/W5/W6, which is noise relative to the estimate.
